name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic network activity across social media platforms, the researcher's signature methodological contribution (CooRnet, CLSB) spanning elections, health topics and information operations.

name: Disinformation Narrative Monitoring
description: Tracking and modeling the propagation of disinformation narratives across Europe (war in Ukraine, LGBTQI+ rights, elections) using language models and monitoring dashboards, central to the PROMPT project and current news on narrative-level fact-checking.

name: AI-Assisted Verification Tools
description: Development of AI-based tools and workflows to help journalists and fact-checkers verify multimedia content and detect coordinated networks, rooted in the vera.ai WP4 leadership and continued through self-updating detection systems.

name: Generative AI and Synthetic Media
description: Study of how generative AI is reshaping visual persuasion, deceptive campaigns, and information operations (e.g. synthetic gambling promotion, deepfakes), reflecting a growing current research and teaching focus (IA Generativa e Media course).

name: Platform Data Access and Research Infrastructure
description: Critical and methodological work on how researchers access and analyze platform data (Meta URL Shares Dataset, CrowdTangle shutdown, clean rooms, APIs under the DSA, open-source sampling tools), a recurring concern given the loss of CrowdTangle access.

name: Political Polarization and Partisanship
description: Analysis of partisan communities, affective polarization, hyperpartisan networks and cross-partisan media exposure on social platforms, a long-running and continuing thread from Bolsonaro networks to Italian and Latin American cases.

name: Italian Election Media Studies
description: The MINE programme's core empirical focus: mapping Italian news media and social media dynamics around national elections (2018, 2022) and related campaigns, providing the longitudinal backbone of the researcher's work.

name: LLMs in Computational Content Analysis
description: Methodological research on integrating and validating large language models for text classification, annotation, and clustering in political and media discourse studies, an active and rapidly growing agenda item.

name: Health Misinformation Networks
description: Mapping coordinated networks and alternative influence structures that circulate problematic health information (COVID-19, vaccine and gatekeeping issues) across Italy, India and Nigeria.

name: Platform Governance and Content Policy
description: Examination of platform moderation and content-distribution policies (Meta's political content reduction, algorithmic governance of the newsfeed, the shift to 'walled garden' platforms) and their effects on visibility and public discourse.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.
